title: 2026-12-07 echosearch hosted api embeddings + rerank demo
summary: Redwood AE and SE walked EchoSearch through the hosted embeddings and reranking endpoints. Focus was improving search relevance for product and help-center search using an embeddings index plus on-the-fly reranking. Covered architecture, demo timings, latency/cost levers, security (SOC 2/SAML/KMS/data retention), and pilot scope. Agreed next steps: send pricing, security pack, sandbox access, and benchmark scripts for a 2-week pilot.
topics: Security: SOC 2 / SAML / KMS / data retention
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Dani (Redwood SE), Jordan (EchoSearch Eng), Priya (EchoSearch PM), Marcus (DS), Tara (Security)

00:00 Alex (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, we can give a 30-40 minute walkthrough of the hosted embeddings + rerank flow then save 10 minutes for Qs
00:12 Jordan: yep that works for us, thanks alex
00:20 Priya: we've been struggling with product search relevance esp multi-term queries and help center docs, curious to see how rerank can improve clickthroughs
00:34 Alex: great, quick agenda 	6 overview, demo in console + API, latency/cost tradeoffs, security notes, pilot options
00:50 Samir (SE): i'll jump into a live demo, show embedding generation, indexing (we'll use the hosted embeddings endpoint), then the reranker which calls the model to re-score candidates
01:10 Marcus: quick Q 	6 are you showing hosted or dedicated? we are leaning hosted for now but might go dedicated later
01:22 Alex: hosted for this demo; architecture supports Dedicated and Private, we can map out what changes later
01:35 Samir: ok pulling up the console 	6 forgive me if autoscroll pops, the console shows an embeddings endpoint key, model list, and an index we created for the demo
01:52 Samir: (typing) first step: call POST /v1/embeddings with text payload, get a vector 	6 here's sample response
02:10 Samir: then we take those vectors into an index 	6 you can use Redwood's hosted index or third parties like Pinecone, weaviate; for today's flow we'll use a simple nearest-neighbor index hosted with EchoSearch locally for the demo to show rerank on top
02:35 Jordan: is the vector index managed by Redwood when using hosted service?
02:42 Dani: if you use Redwood's managed index, yes we host it and manage scaling/replicas; otherwise you can push vectors to any vector DB. For rerank we support taking candidate ids and calling the rerank endpoint to re-score with context
03:00 Priya: show the rerank payload 	6 is it a pairwise format or list of documents?
03:08 Samir: good Q 	6 we support a ranked-candidate list payload: you send query + topK candidate texts or ids + optional metadata, the reranker returns scores and reordered list. It's flexible: you can do pairwise or multi-candidate; multi is more efficient for small K
03:30 Samir: example POST /v1/rerank body: {query: "...", candidates: [{id, text, doc_meta}, ...], context: {user_profile}} 	6 response contains scores and rationales if enabled
03:50 Marcus: rationale? as in explainability output?
03:56 Samir: yes optional field, model will output short rationale strings, but it increases token usage and latency
04:10 Tara (Security): real quick on data: what gets logged and retained for hosted flows? we need to know for compliance
04:18 Alex: good call 	6 hosted API has configurable retention: by default we retain minimal logs for billing and debugging, and you can opt into no retention. We also support customer-managed keys (KMS) for encryption at rest and SAML SSO for admin access. We'll send the SOC 2 pack after the call
04:40 Tara: ok thanks, we'll want to see audit log samples
04:48 Samir: jumping back to demo 	6 i'll run a sample where the query is 'how do I change billing address' and topK from embeddings returns 8 candidates, then rerank pushes the most relevant doc to top
05:05 Samir: (runs request, shows timings) embeddings call ~40 ms, index lookup ~12 ms, rerank call ~120-180 ms depending on model and tokens. end-to-end ~250-400 ms in demo env
05:30 Jordan: 120-180 for rerank is fine if we only rerank top 8, but our SLA target is sub-200 ms total for product search 	6 any ways to reduce that?
05:43 Dani: couple levers: use smaller reranker model (faster), enable KV prefix caching for repeated queries, do batching for many parallel queries, or use hybrid approach: use embeddings similarity to get a strong candidate then only rerank top 3 for strict latency SLO
06:10 Marcus: are there pre-quantization options to speed rerank? we have hardware constraints later if dedicated
06:18 Samir: on Dedicated we can run quantized models and tune sequence length; for hosted we provide optimized kernels 	6 smaller model choices often get you below 100 ms rerank for short inputs
06:36 Priya: can we see a before/after for relevance metrics?
06:40 Samir: i prepared a simple search test 	6 baseline embeddings-only rerank off, then rerank on. Showing MR@1 and CTR lifts (toy dataset) 	6 MR@1 improves from 0.62 to 0.79, clickthrough simulated +15%
07:05 Jordan: nice, what's the sample size?
07:08 Samir: toy set ~2k queries; for a production pilot we'd run a larger A/B and log real clicks, we'll provide the eval harness
07:20 Alex: that's part of Redwood Optimize 	6 we can suggest model profiles and quantizations for your workload and run cost estimates
07:30 Priya: show console for Optimize
07:35 Dani: (screenshare) Optimize dashboard takes your query distribution, suggests batch sizes, caching TTLs, and recommends model variant with cost/latency tradeoffs. Here it suggests rerank-small for help docs and rerank-base for product catalog
07:58 Jordan: curious about throughput 	6 we have spikes during launches, can hosted autoscale handle bursts?
08:05 Alex: hosted autoscaling manages burst capacity; for predictable sustained throughput you can move to Dedicated reserved pools with SLA and configurable burst policy
08:18 Tara: on the security side, if we choose hosted, can we enforce VPC peering or private networking?
08:25 Alex: yes 	6 hosted private link options exist for enterprise, and Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) is available for strict network boundaries
08:36 Marcus: what about data residency? some docs must stay in EU
08:40 Dani: we support region pinning for models and hosted indices; we'll record region in the request metadata and can configure storage to EU regions only
08:50 Priya: demo 	6 can you show adding metadata like product_id and category to candidates and rerank taking that into account?
08:58 Samir: sure 	6 i'll show the candidate objects include metadata and you can add weighting in reranker by signal. Running demo now
09:20 Samir: (runs) we add category boosting in call, top doc jumps when product_id matches. showing logs and explanation in console
09:40 Jordan: transcripts sometimes mis-parse product names, curious how robust model is to entity variants
09:45 Samir: you can add aliases in index and use metadata mapping; reranker can be primed with alias list as context too
09:55 Priya: okay let's talk pricing 	6 approximate for 100k queries per day with average 15 tokens per rerank call and embeddings?
10:03 Alex: high-level: embeddings are per-vector unit, rerank is per-token and per-request. we'll send a detailed pricing sheet; rough back-of-envelope for your volume we'll include in follow-up
10:20 Jordan: what about running local benchmarks? can we get sample scripts?
10:24 Dani: yes SE will share a benchmark script and a small dataset. we'll also open a sandbox account with 100k credits for pilot
10:35 Marcus: about evaluation 	6 can Redwood's console show latency breakdown per token and per-route?
10:42 Dani: yes, Console has per-route latency histograms, token-level cost breakdowns, and traces to map slow hops. You can set alerts on regressions as part of Optimize
10:56 Tara: SOC 2 	6 you said you'd send security pack, does Redwood have ISO as well?
11:02 Alex: SOC 2 Type II is available, ISO 27001 in progress; we'll attach docs. Also we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and customer-managed KMS
11:20 Priya: next steps for pilot and success metrics? we want CTR lift and MR@1 improvement, sub-200 ms p95 for product search, and security approval by Dec 21
11:33 Alex: noted. we'll aim to support that timeline. SE to provide pilot plan and benchmark script, Security pack to Tara
11:45 Jordan: any objections from engineering on ingesting vectors? we use Kafka pipeline today
11:50 Samir: the index ingest can be batched and pushed via API; we also support streaming ingestion with a connector 	6 will share the connector guide
12:05 Priya: can rerank be combined with personalization signal? we have user profiles and recency weights
12:12 Dani: yes you can pass user_profile in context or store per-doc features in metadata for the reranker to use. Optimize can recommend feature weighting defaults
12:33 Marcus: what about A/B and rollouts?
12:36 Alex: Console supports rule-based rollouts, canary traffic, and automatic fallback to a cheaper model if latency spikes
12:50 Priya: any notes on limits for embeddings dimension or vector size?
12:55 Samir: we support common dims up to 2048; higher dims increase storage/costs, Optimize will recommend dims by workload
13:10 Tara: thanks everyone, i need to review the security pdf; please include data deletion SLA
13:15 Alex: yes data deletion SLA and retention controls will be in the security pack
13:25 Priya: are there example notebooks for rerank evaluation?
13:30 Dani: yes we'll include a Jupyter notebook with evaluation harness and example metrics (MR@k, NDCG, CTR estimate)
13:40 Alex: ok quick recap and actions
13:45 Jordan: great thanks, this was useful
13:50 Alex: thanks all

Note: timestamps are approximate; the call continued with Q&A and wrap-up to match the 42 minute duration.
next_steps: Send detailed pricing sheet for 100k qps/day estimate
Share SOC 2/ISO security pack and audit log samples
SE to provide benchmark script and sample dataset
Provision sandbox account with 100k credits for EchoSearch pilot
